title: Pluggable LLM providers and production-cycle dashboard
criteriaSource: Phase 17 prompt acceptance criteria P17-AC01..AC18, extended by the Product Owner acceptance contract to AC19..AC32 (AC31 split into AC31a/AC31b)
purpose: Registered so no criterion silently loses its implementation or test.

status 'done' requires real implementation and a real test; 'partial' means implemented but the criterion's full evidence is missing (see note); 'not-applicable' is only for the branch the owner did not choose.
tests/regression/p17-traceability.check.cjs fails on any done or partial row whose paths or tests do not exist.

verifiedByMeaning.test: An executing regression test asserts the criterion.
verifiedByMeaning.platform: Third-party platform behaviour; Falcon wiring tested, outcome evidenced on hosted runs.
verifiedByMeaning.review: Evidenced by a recorded review verdict or scan output rather than code.

criteria.title: Explicit provider selection
criteria.text: Supported providers openai, azure-openai, openai-compatible, disabled; case-sensitive, validated, deterministic; unset means no provider contact

tests.name: AC01: unset provider resolves to disabled, zero provider contact
AC01: same config resolves to the same selection
registry exact-match lookup is case-sensitive, no fuzzy match

criteria.title: OpenAI adapter
criteria.text: provider=openai preserves the Tier 3 request shape and numeric-only reply contract; healing tests pass unmodified through a stub provider

tests.name: (1) real SDK through guardedFetch: auth header, identity encoding, no org/project headers, body shape
real provider replying '3' is chosen after live re-verification; recordTier3Invocation called once
registry: provider=openai resolves to a wired OpenAIProvider instance (Dev-02a)

criteria.title: Azure OpenAI adapter
criteria.text: Deployment is sent as model against https://<resource>.<suffix>/openai/v1/ with key authentication; Entra ID excluded

tests.name: (AzureOpenAIProvider) AC03/AC20: path is /openai/v1/chat/completions, body.model is the deployment, Bearer auth, no api-version

criteria.note: Owner-accepted disposition: verified against a contract-complete mock (path, deployment as model, key authentication, no api-version); no live Azure resource was available and Entra ID authentication is out of scope. Remains partial.

criteria.title: OpenAI-compatible adapter
criteria.text: Requires explicit operator opt-in; works against a loopback mock; non-opted-in or unsafe endpoints make zero requests

tests.name: AC04: openai-compatible without allowCustomEndpoint=true returns CONFIG_ENDPOINT_OPT_IN_REQUIRED, zero I/O
AC04: opt-in but loopback http not allowed is rejected with zero connections
openai-compatible without opt-in flag -> CONFIG_ENDPOINT_OPT_IN_REQUIRED, zero requests

criteria.title: Provider isolation
criteria.text: With instrumented mock endpoints only the selected provider receives requests; all others receive exactly zero

tests.name: AC05: each provider only ever talks to its own loopback server, never the other two
AC05: registry.resolve builds exactly one provider class per id, never the others

criteria.title: No-provider behaviour
criteria.text: Without a provider Tier 1/2/2.5 and local healing continue; Tier 3 returns null non-fatally with a warning code

tests.name: AC06: disabled provider is consulted but constructs no client, no network
CONFIG_PROVIDER_REQUIRED: no provider configured => null, no SDK/factory call, no Tier3 trust record

criteria.title: Approval and trust preservation
criteria.text: Provider output never bypasses local validation, Phase 8 approval, quarantine or reuse rules; HealingTrust is unchanged

tests.name: a valid index acts on the built selector and still records pending trust
a free-form selector reply is rejected and nothing is clicked
an out-of-range index is rejected
rejected reply (${label}) => null, nothing approved, rejection reason unchanged
BUDGET_EXHAUSTED: canSend() false => no Tier3 trust record and complete() never called

criteria.title: Data minimisation
criteria.text: Outbound payload is at most 20 candidates and 8192 bytes; planted markers outside candidate context never reach the wire

tests.name: prompt bounds (S-09): <=20 candidate lines, <=8192 bytes, index mapping preserved
prompt bounds with multibyte candidate text: byte cap holds, trailing candidates dropped whole
data minimisation + redaction (AC08/S-17): markers in cookie/hidden-DOM/localStorage/env never reach prompt, request, logs, or report

criteria.title: Safe, distinguishable failures
criteria.text: Missing or invalid config, 401, 429, timeout, network, malformed, oversized and unsupported provider produce distinct codes with no secret leakage

tests.name: (${name}) AC09 fixture: 401 -> AUTH_FAILED, never retried
(${name}) AC09 fixture: oversized response -> OVERSIZED
closed error-code list is frozen and matches ADR-0017 section 5
numeric bounds: out-of-range FALCON_LLM_TIMEOUT_MS -> CONFIG_INVALID

criteria.title: Honest telemetry
criteria.text: Reports carry provider, model label, latency, outcome and normalised error code only; no prompts, keys, URLs or DOM

tests.name: S-10: telemetry serializes a success result from the allowlist only
extra/unknown fields on the input never survive serialization
S-16: escapeHtml neutralises HTML/script content for report rendering
real provider result attaches an allowlisted llm telemetry block to the report row

criteria.title: Benchmark provider dimension
criteria.text: Phase 14 benchmark reports no-key and provider-protocol rows separately; mock rows are labelled protocol compatibility only

tests.name: claimScope is a frozen, exact string
buildProviderDimension: quality rates are identical with and without mock rows (no-key numbers unchanged)
formatProviderDimensionText: labels mock rows with claimScope and never emits comparative/superiority wording
runProviderProtocolRows: a REAL round trip hits the loopback mock server and records protocol success

criteria.note: Owner-approved disposition: the criterion wording requires separately labelled no-key and provider rows without presenting mock compatibility as model quality, which is met. promptCoverage at 20 versus 60 candidates is not part of the wording and stays an unmeasured, documented limit (the Tier 2.5 corpus has no Tier 3 ranking data).

criteria.title: Real coordination dashboard
criteria.text: Dashboard renders actual persisted ledger events with models, sender, recipient, task, revision, evidence, state, blocker and verdict, refreshing within 2 seconds

tests.name: AC12/AC13: page loads, 12 roles + coordinator, LIVE, event ids map
AC12: complete triple shows routed card; incomplete shows awaiting
GET /api/state returns combined shape

criteria.title: No fabricated communication
criteria.text: Every visible message maps to one persisted event id; no chain-of-thought fields exist

tests.name: AC12/AC13: page loads, 12 roles + coordinator, LIVE, event ids map
UI: no chain-of-thought field names read as properties
unknown top-level key is rejected

criteria.title: Dashboard security
criteria.text: Loopback-only, read-only, escaped, bounded, redacted, path-safe; cannot expose repository or .git content

tests.name: D-11: missing/invalid Host header is 403
D-13: connection hardening options are applied
405 matrix: non-GET methods return Allow: GET
D-19: non-loopback host rejected at create
UI: forbidden DOM-injection APIs are absent
resolveRunDir rejects a symlinked run directory
a line with no newline that outgrows the line limit is dropped, not buffered

criteria.title: Governance consistency
criteria.text: Model policy, agent files and docs agree; Fable prohibited; only the two documented reuse pairs

tests.name: AC15: CLAUDE.md routing table == house-doc table == agent front matter
AC15: exactly two reuse pairs, other six distinct
AC15: no stray fable mention outside prohibition contexts

criteria.title: Security gate (GitHub Advanced Security)
criteria.text: GitHub Advanced Security is the authoritative gate: CodeQL JavaScript/TypeScript and Actions analyses green on the final head, the pull-request code-scanning result has zero unresolved alerts, and GitHub secret-scanning results are clean where available; npm audit is dependency-hygiene evidence and GitGuardian is advisory. Third-party scanners are not applicable by owner security policy
criteria.note: Owner-approved governance change (not a scan result): the earlier requirement for third-party scanner evidence is removed and those fields are NOT APPLICABLE — excluded by owner security policy. Evidence is the hosted CodeQL (JavaScript/TypeScript and Actions) and PR code-scanning results on the final head, read from GitHub and recorded in the pull request and the release record.

criteria.title: Compatibility and regression
criteria.text: Existing non-provider behaviour and public interfaces stay compatible; documented breaking changes only

tests.name: a type action fills the chosen field only
rejection logs a report row with reason and status and persists nothing
CONFIG_PROVIDER_REQUIRED: no provider configured => null, no SDK/factory call, no Tier3 trust record

criteria.title: Operator documentation
criteria.text: Configuration, privacy boundary, provider examples, dashboard use, limitations, rollback and troubleshooting are accurate; env examples genuinely blank

tests.name: numeric bounds: unset settings fall back to ADR defaults

criteria.note: Prose accuracy is evidenced by the Code Reviewer verdicts; the defaults quoted in .env.example and the operations guide are pinned to the code by the config test.

criteria.title: Configuration negatives
criteria.text: Blank provider is unset; wrong-case or unknown values fail with zero requests; conflicting settings and unknown FALCON_LLM_ keys are reported

tests.name: AC19: blank provider is treated as unset
AC19: conflicting settings (AZURE_* with non-azure provider) -> CONFIG_CONFLICT
AC19: unknown FALCON_LLM_* key logs one warning naming the key

criteria.title: Endpoint policy
criteria.text: https only except opted-in loopback http; metadata and link-local always denied; private ranges, IPv4-mapped forms, userinfo, rebinding and redirects are rejected

tests.name: always-deny: AWS IMDS v6 stays denied even with allowPrivate+allowLoopback+extraAllowedPorts
IPv4-mapped ::ffff:169.254.169.254 is always denied regardless of opts
assertAllResolvedAllowed rejects the whole lookup if any resolved address is denied
redirect response is rejected and never followed
DNS-rebinding: second resolution is never used, pinned address is the one connected
mixed resolved answers (public + private) are rejected with zero connections
hostname endpoint connects through the pinned lookup (Node { all: true } contract)

criteria.title: Concurrent Tier 3 calls
criteria.text: Two concurrent calls do not cross-talk and the concurrency cap holds

tests.name: AC21: two concurrent complete() calls each get their own result, mock sees exactly 2 requests
AC21: concurrency cap of 1 serialises two complete() calls on one provider instance

criteria.title: Concurrent ledger appends
criteria.text: Concurrent appends through the append primitive yield parseable, chained, non-duplicated events

tests.name: AC22: two writers x200 appendEvent into one run dir produce 400 valid chained events
SIGKILL variant: a stale lock left by a killed holder is recoverable

criteria.note: Retargeted from N cross-process writers to the append primitive under concurrent invocation because the coordinator is the sole ledger writer; accepted by QA.

criteria.title: Planted markers never leak
criteria.text: Planted keys, headers, prompts and tokens appear zero times in logs, reports, ledger, dashboard and errors

tests.name: D-22: M06 short hostile HTML is accepted by Redact, stays a plain escaped string
pattern review: ghp_ GitHub token is refused
DEF-01: ${variantName} is refused in summary
M07: secret written directly into a line's summary field never leaks
error message and Logger output never contain a planted marker

criteria.title: Retry, budget and backoff
criteria.text: Attempts per call are bounded, backoff is capped, a per-run budget returns BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, 400/401 are never retried

tests.name: AC24: continuous 429 -> attempts == maxAttempts(2), mock sees exactly 2 requests, 400 never retried
AC24: continuous 500 -> attempts == maxAttempts(2), budget exhaustion stops further requests
RetryPolicy: never retries AUTH_FAILED or BAD_REQUEST

criteria.note: The call budget is per process; with N workers the effective ceiling is N times the budget.

tests.name: hang times out within bound
